title: From His Healings to His Betrayal
english: “…has stood against Me? Or who will stand against Me and endure?” (Job 41:10-11)

33. That He will heal many. Isaiah says, “Be strong, you drooping hands and feeble knees; give comfort, you who are faint of heart; do not be afraid” (Isaiah 35:3-4). And again, “Then God will come; then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will hear; then the lame will leap like a deer, and the tongue of those who stammer will speak clearly” (Isaiah 35:4-6).
34. That He will raise the dead. Isaiah says, “Death, grown strong, swallowed up; and again God has taken away every tear from every face” (Isaiah 25:8).

35. That the Jews will not believe. Isaiah says, “Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?” (Isaiah 53:1). “Those to whom nothing was announced about him will see, and those who have not heard will understand” (Isaiah 52:15).

36. That from five loaves He will feed many. Isaiah says, “On that day they will say: Behold, our God; we have hoped and rejoiced in our salvation, for God will give rest on this mountain” (Isaiah 25:9-10).

37. That He will enter Zion on a donkey. Zechariah says, “Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion; proclaim, daughter of Jerusalem, for your king is coming to you, righteous and gentle, mounted on a beast of burden and a young colt” (Zechariah 9:9). And Jacob says, “Binding his donkey to the vine” (Genesis 49:11). And Malachi says, “Suddenly the Lord whom you desire will come to His temple, and the messenger of the covenant” (Malachi 3:1).

38. That the little children will run ahead of Him, crying, “Blessed is He who comes” (Psalm 118:26; Matthew 21:9). David says in the 8th Psalm, “Out of the mouth of infants and nursing babies You have perfected praise” (Psalm 8:2).

39. That He will rebuke the people. Malachi says, “I will draw near to you in judgment, and I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers, against the adulteresses, and against those who swear by falsehoods” (Malachi 3:5). And Jeremiah says, “Is My house a den of robbers? And has My name been called over them?” (Jeremiah 7:11).
40. That nard will be poured over Him. In the Song of Songs it says, “While the king reclined at his table, nard gave forth its fragrance” (Song of Solomon 1:12).

41. That they will gather together against Him. David says in the 2nd Psalm, “Why did the nations rage, and the peoples plot vain things? The kings of the earth took their stand, and the rulers gathered together against the Lord and against His Christ” (Psalm 2:1-2). And again he says in the 3rd Psalm, “Lord, why have those who afflict me multiplied? Many rise up against me; many say to my soul, ‘There is no salvation for him in his God’” (Psalm 3:1-2). And Jeremiah says, “The Spirit before our face, Christ the Lord, was seized in our corruptions, of whom we said, ‘In his shadow we shall live’” (Lamentations 4:20). And again he says, “For they set their hands to words to seize me, and laid snares for me. And You, Lord, have known all their counsel against me for my death; do not hold their wrongs guiltless, and do not blot out their sins from Your sight” (Jeremiah 18:22-23).

42. That they will bear false witness against Him. David says in the 35th Psalm, “Unjust witnesses rose up against me; they questioned me about things I did not know; they repaid me evil for good” (Psalm 35:11-12). And again he says in the 59th Psalm, “Rescue me from my enemies, O God, and redeem me from those who rise up against me; deliver me from those who work lawlessness, and save me from men of blood” (Psalm 59:1-2).

43. That Judas will betray Him. David says in the 41st Psalm, “My enemies spoke evil of me: ‘When will he die, and his name perish?’ And he came in to see; he spoke empty words; his heart gathered lawlessness for itself; he went outside and spoke. All my enemies whispered together against me; against me they devised evil for me; they laid a lawless word against me” (Psalm 41:5-8). And again, “He who eats my bread has raised his heel high against me” (Psalm 41:9). And again he says in the 52nd Psalm, “Why do you boast in wickedness, O mighty one, in lawlessness all day long? Your tongue has devised injustice; like a sharpened razor you have worked deceit; you have loved wickedness more than goodness” (Psalm 52:1-3). And again he says in the 38th Psalm, “My friends and my neighbors drew near and stood opposite me” (Psalm 38:11).

44. That Judas will say, “Greetings, Rabbi” (Matthew 26:49). David says in the 55th Psalm, “His words were softer than oil, yet they are darts. Cast your care upon the Lord, and He will sustain you” (Psalm 55:21-22). And again he says in the 109th Psalm, “O God, do not pass over my praise in silence, for the mouth of the sinner and the mouth of the deceitful has been opened against me” (Psalm 109:1-2).
45. That He will be sold for silver. Zechariah says, “I will say to them: If it is good in your sight, give me my wages, thirty pieces of silver” (Zechariah 11:12).

translator_notes: The section opens with the end of Job 41:10-11, begun at the close of the previous section.
In this section the Psalm numbers in the running text follow the English numbering; Epiphanius’s Greek numbers are one lower (34, 58, 40, 51, 37, 54, 108).
41.1: the edition reads “their Christ” in Psalm 2:2, an evident slip for “His Christ”, which the Greek of the Psalm has.
41.3 is Lamentations 4:20, which Epiphanius gives under Jeremiah’s name, as at 5.29.
41.4: the edition’s verb for the snares is read as “hid”, as in the Greek of Jeremiah 18:22; rendered “laid snares”.

title: Arrest, Trial and Crucifixion
english: And Jeremiah says, “They gave the thirty pieces of silver, the price of the one on whom a price was set, whom some of the sons of Israel priced; and they gave them for the potter’s field” (Matthew 27:9-10; Zechariah 11:13).

46. That they will bind Him. Isaiah says, “Woe to your soul, for they have taken evil counsel against themselves, saying, ‘Let us bind the righteous man, for he is troublesome to us’” (Isaiah 3:9-10). And Solomon says, “Let us lie in wait for the righteous man, for he is troublesome to us; he is a burden to us even to look at” (Wisdom of Solomon 2:12, 14).

47. That they will put Him on trial. David says in the 69th Psalm, “Save me, O God, for the waters have come in up to my soul. I am stuck fast in the mire of the deep, and there is no foothold” (Psalm 69:1-2). And again he says in the 71st Psalm, “In You, Lord, I have hoped; let me never be put to shame. In Your righteousness rescue me and deliver me,” and so on (Psalm 71:1-2). And Isaiah says, “Against whom have you opened your mouth? And against whom have you let loose your tongue? Against whom but the gentle, the humble and the quiet?” (Isaiah 57:4; 66:2). And again, “My inheritance has become to me like a lion in the forest; it has raised its voice against me; therefore I have hated it” (Jeremiah 12:8). “It was not I who refused; it was they who refused me. Therefore I have forsaken my house” (Jeremiah 12:7).

48. That they will strike Him and treat Him with contempt. Micah says, “They will strike the judge of Israel on the cheek” (Micah 5:1). And, “The one abhorred by the nations, by the servants of rulers: kings will see him, and rulers will rise up and worship him” (Isaiah 49:7). And elsewhere he says, “But I do not disobey, nor do I answer back. I have given my back to the whip and my cheeks to blows, and I did not turn my face away from the shame of spitting” (Isaiah 50:5-6).

49. That the apostles will flee. David says in the 38th Psalm, “My friends and my neighbors drew near and stood opposite me” (Psalm 38:11). And again, “You have put my acquaintances far from me” (Psalm 88:8). And, “I looked for someone to grieve with me, and there was none, and for someone to comfort me, and I found none” (Psalm 69:20).
50. That Peter will deny Him. Isaiah says, “And he was afraid of mortal man, of those who will wither like grass; but he has forgotten Me, says the Lord” (Isaiah 51:12-13).

51. That they will crucify Him. Jeremiah says, “But I was like an innocent lamb led to be sacrificed” (Jeremiah 11:19). And Isaiah says, “He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer” (Isaiah 53:7). And Wisdom says, “Let us condemn him to a shameful death” (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). And again, “Come, let us put wood into his bread, and let us wipe him out from the land of the living” (Jeremiah 11:19). And David says, “They pierced my hands and my feet” (Psalm 22:16).

52. That they will crown Him with thorns. In the Song of Songs it says, “Go out and look, daughters of Jerusalem, at the crown with which his mother crowned him” (Song of Solomon 3:11). And Isaiah says, “I waited for it to yield grapes, but it yielded thorns” (Isaiah 5:4).

53. That they will give Him vinegar and gall to drink (Psalm 69:21). David says in the 69th Psalm, “They gave me gall for my food, and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink” (Psalm 69:21). And Moses says, “Is this how you repay the Lord?” (Deuteronomy 32:6). And in the Song of Songs it says, “He came into my garden, my sister, my bride, and they gathered my myrrh” (Song of Solomon 5:1). And again, “My hands dripped with myrrh, and my fingers were full of myrrh” (Song of Solomon 5:5). And again it says, “I will give you spiced wine to drink” (Song of Solomon 8:2).

54. That they will clothe Him in a scarlet robe. Isaiah says, “Who is this who comes from Edom, the red of his garments from Bozrah, this one splendid in his robe, with might? Why are your garments red, and your clothing as if from a trodden winepress?” (Isaiah 63:1-2).

55. That He will keep silent when He is tried. David says in the 38th Psalm, “I became like a man who does not hear and who has no rebukes in his mouth” (Psalm 38:14). And again, “But I, like a deaf man, did not hear, and was like a mute man who does not open his mouth” (Psalm 38:13). And Isaiah says, “And he, because he has been afflicted, does not open his mouth; like a sheep he was led to the slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer, so he does not open his mouth in his humiliation” (Isaiah 53:7-8).

56. That He will be mocked. David says in the 109th Psalm, “They saw me; they shook their heads” (Psalm 109:25). And in Wisdom it says, “If he is a righteous son of God, He will help him” (Wisdom of Solomon 2:18). “He claims to have knowledge of God, and calls himself a child of the Lord” (Wisdom of Solomon 2:13).
57. That He who hangs on the tree is Himself the Life. Moses says, “Your life will hang on a tree before your eyes, and you will be afraid day and…” (Deuteronomy 28:66)
translator_notes: 45.2: Epiphanius, following Matthew 27:9-10, gives the words under Jeremiah’s name; the prophecy is Zechariah 11:13.
In this section the Psalm numbers in the running text follow the English numbering; Epiphanius’s Greek numbers are one lower (68, 70, 37, 108).
46.1 keeps the edition’s “Woe to your soul”, where the Greek of Isaiah 3:9 has “their soul”.
47.4: “It was not I who refused; it was they who refused me” has no exact match in the Greek of Jeremiah 12; it stands beside Jeremiah 12:7-8 and is cited there.
51.4 is introduced with “And again” after Wisdom, but the words are Jeremiah 11:19.
The section ends in the middle of Deuteronomy 28:66, as the source does; the next section carries the rest.

title: Death, Burial and Resurrection
english: “…night, and you will not believe in your life” (Deuteronomy 28:66). And again he says, “Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree” (Deuteronomy 21:23).

58. That His suffering is freedom from suffering. Isaiah cries out, saying, “We reckoned him to be in pain and stricken; but he was wounded for our iniquities and weakened for our sins; the chastisement that brought our peace was upon him, and by his bruise we have all been healed” (Isaiah 53:4-5). And Sirach says, “They beat me, and I felt no pain” (Proverbs 23:35). And David says in the 64th Psalm, “Their blows have become like children’s arrows” (Psalm 64:7).

59. That Christ will suffer at night, while it is cold and a charcoal fire has been laid (John 18:18). Zechariah says, “And on that day there will be cold, and there will be frost for one day” (Zechariah 14:6-7).

60. That the sun will set. Zechariah is the first to say, “And on that day there will be no light; that day is known to the Lord, and it will be neither day nor night, and toward evening there will be light” (Zechariah 14:6-7). And Joel says, “Before his face the earth will be gathered together, and the heaven will be darkened; sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will withdraw their brightness” (Joel 2:10).

61. That the sun will set at noon (Amos 8:9). Amos says, “And on that day, says the Lord God, the sun will set at noon, and its light will grow dark on the earth by day, and He will turn our feasts into mourning” (Amos 8:9-10).
62. That they will divide His garments among themselves (Psalm 22:18). David says in the 22nd Psalm, “They divided my garments among themselves, and for my clothing they cast lots” (Psalm 22:18).
63. That He will be crucified with robbers. Isaiah says, “And he was numbered with the lawless, and his soul was handed over to death” (Isaiah 53:12).
64. That they will pierce His side. Zechariah says, “They will look on him whom they pierced” (Zechariah 12:10).
65. That not one of His bones will be broken (Exodus 12:46; John 19:36). Moses says, “No bone of his will be broken” (Exodus 12:46; Numbers 9:12).
66. That water will flow from His side as a figure of baptism. Isaiah says, “Bread will be given to him, and his water will be sure” (Isaiah 33:16).
67. That He will be laid in a rock. Isaiah says, “Look to the solid rock that you hewed, and to the hollow of the pit that you dug” (Isaiah 51:1).
68. That the door of the tomb is a stone. He also says, “And they laid a stone upon me” (Lamentations 3:53).

69. That they will set a seal on Him. Daniel says, “And they brought a single stone and laid it on the mouth of the pit, and the king sealed it with his ring and with the ring of his nobles, so that nothing might be changed in the case of Daniel” (Daniel 6:17).

70. That His passion will take place as summer begins, in the month we call March. In the Song of Songs it says, “The season has passed; the nations have gone their way. He has appeared on the earth; the time of pruning has come” (Song of Solomon 2:11-12).

71. That He will be buried. Isaiah says, “The righteous man has been taken away from the presence of injustice; his burial will be in peace” (Isaiah 57:1-2). And again he says, “Because of the sins of my people he was led to death; and I will give the wicked in return for his burial and the rich in return for his death” (Isaiah 53:8-9). And Jacob says, “Lying down, he slept like a lion and like a lion’s cub; who will rouse him?” (Genesis 49:9). And in Numbers it says, “Lying down, he rested like a lion and like a lion’s cub” (Numbers 24:9). And David says in the 22nd Psalm, “You have brought me down to the dust of death” (Psalm 22:15).

72. That, once buried, He will strike Hades with fear. In Job it says, “The gates of death will be opened to him in fear, and the gatekeepers of Hades cowered when they saw you” (Job 38:17). And Isaiah says, “Hades below was embittered when it met you” (Isaiah 14:9). And David says in the 107th Psalm, “He shattered gates of bronze and crushed bars of iron” (Psalm 107:16).
73. That He is without sin. Isaiah says, “He committed no sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth” (Isaiah 53:9). And again, “Because of the sins of my people he was led to death” (Isaiah 53:8).

74. That He will rise again. David says in the 12th Psalm, “Because of the misery of the poor and the groaning of the needy, now I will arise, says the Lord” (Psalm 12:5). And again he says in the 16th Psalm, “For You will not abandon my soul to Hades, nor will You let Your Holy One see corruption” (Psalm 16:10). And again he says in the 30th Psalm, “You brought up my soul from Hades, from among those who go down into the pit” (Psalm 30:3). And Jeremiah says, “Therefore I awoke, and behold, my sleep became sweet” (Jeremiah 31:26). And David says in the 88th Psalm, “By day I cried out, and by night before You; I was counted among those who go down into the pit” (Psalm 88:1, 4). And again, “I have become like…” (Psalm 88:4-5)
translator_notes: The section begins and ends in the middle of a verse (Deuteronomy 28:66; Psalm 88:4-5), as the source does.

In this section the Psalm numbers in the running text follow the English numbering; Epiphanius’s Greek numbers are one lower. At 62.1 the printed “61st” is a slip for 21 (Psalm 22), and at 72.3 the printed “100th” has lost a digit and stands for 106 (Psalm 107).
58.2: Epiphanius names Sirach; the words are Proverbs 23:35, and the citation gives Proverbs.

70.1: the edition reads “the nations” where the Greek of Song of Solomon 2:12 has “the flowers”; the edition’s reading is kept, and the singular verb that follows is given the subject “He”. The reading is uncertain.
The numbers 70 and 71 here follow the body of the work, where 70 is the passion in March and 71 the burial; the chapter list gives these two headings in the reverse order.
71.1: the edition’s verb is read as “has been taken away”, as in the Greek of Isaiah 57:1. 72.1: the edition’s “spat” is read as “cowered”, as in the Greek of Job 38:17.
